page: Microsoft Azure D8nlds_v6 is a dedicated virtual machine instance within the Dnldv6 series, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs based on Intel processor architecture and 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU, reflecting a low-memory profile tailored for compute-focused requirements rather than memory-heavy footprints. The instance contains zero discrete GPU accelerators, allocating all system capacity directly to standard CPU and memory execution.

Storage capability on the D8nlds_v6 includes an integrated 472 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, which delivers direct high-throughput local storage for scratch files and temporary operations. The instance also supports Azure Premium Storage for attaching persistent remote block volumes. Classified within the network-optimized tier, it is structured to manage higher network throughput demands. It is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual network interfaces for external address assignment.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides cost efficiency for processing-heavy workloads by minimizing expenditure on unused RAM. The primary tradeoff is the constrained memory capacity of 16.0 GB across 8 cores, which limits suitability for memory-resident databases or expansive analytic datasets. Microsoft Azure D8nlds_v6 is technically suited for continuous integration runners, web serving, network edge services, batch processing, and distributed application tasks that require dedicated CPU execution alongside rapid local NVMe temporary storage.

Microsoft Azure D8nlds_v6 is appropriate for compute-bound tasks, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, intermediate data processing, distributed network services, and application caching requiring fast local scratch disks.
